title: Asif Hameed v State of Jammu and Kashmir

content.caseIdentity: Asif Hameed & Ors. v. State of Jammu & Kashmir & Ors., 1989 Supp (2) SCC 364; AIR 1989 SC 1899; 1989 SCR (3) 19
content.facts: Unsuccessful candidates challenged the 1988-89 MBBS/BDS selections in Jammu and Kashmir. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court had treated earlier observations in Jyotshana Sharma v. State of Jammu & Kashmir as requiring a statutory independent selection body and had issued directions concerning the selection process. The State and selected candidates appealed, including on the ground that the High Court had exceeded its competence by directing the State to constitute such a statutory body.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the High Court could direct the State Government to constitute a statutory body for selecting candidates for medical colleges.

Whether the High Court could treat its earlier observations concerning an independent selection body as binding directions requiring the State to legislate or reorganise the executive selection process.
Whether the executive selection procedure and selections remained subject to judicial review for constitutional or legal infirmity.
content.ratioDecidendi: The Constitution demarcates the functions of the legislature, executive and judiciary even though separation of powers is not recognised in absolute rigidity. In judicial review of administrative action, a court is not an appellate authority and must remain within self-imposed limits; it cannot direct or advise the executive on policy matters falling within the constitutional sphere of the legislature or executive where those authorities remain within constitutional and statutory limits. Courts cannot direct the legislature to enact legislation. Executive action and selection procedures nevertheless remain open to judicial review for unreasonableness and other constitutional or legal infirmity.
content.holding: The Supreme Court allowed the appeals filed by the State and selected candidates and dismissed the appeals of the unsuccessful candidates. It held that the High Court was in error in directing the State to constitute a statutory independent body and in treating the earlier observations as binding directions. The State's executive could operate in the field in the absence of legislation on medical education, subject to constitutional and legal limits and judicial review.
content.relevance: Authoritative Supreme Court authority for the limits of judicial review, institutional separation, and judicial restraint in matters falling within the legislative or executive policy domain. The decision should not be read as excluding judicial review of executive action; it expressly preserves review for constitutional or legal infirmity and unreasonableness.
